newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW-Bank of Melb sees flat half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW-Bank of Melb sees flat half.

text.p: Bank of Melbourne (BOM) chief executive David Airey said on Monday he expected results for the six months to December 31 to be in line with a year earlier.
"The outlook for full year-end is for a good result. I think coming through in the first half, I think the results will be steady," chief executive officer David Airey told Reuters.
Airey added: "The full impact of Challenge will be felt in the second half and the bank will be removing a good level of cost."
BOM posted a net profit after abnormals of A$44.57 million for the six months to December, 1995. Profit for the full year to June 30 was A$91.21 million, up from A$78.92 million.
Airey said the bank had continued to grow well organically during the fiscal first half and its interstate operations had contributed strongly.
"The long term future for the bank is good," he said.
But the performance of its key market, the state of Victoria, had been relatively flat during the half, he said.

BOM earlier announced it had finalised the purchase of the Victorian assets of Westpac Banking Corp unit Challenge Bank for A$645 million, about A$155 million less than it had originally expected to pay.

BOM also said it had closed 15 Challenge branches and three of its own over the weekend as part of the integration of Challenge. Airey said it was too early to know what savings would flow from the closures. He said BOM was unlikely to close additional branches during the second half.

"The bank has a total of 126 branches now. We're constantly reviewing our branch infrastructure but at this stage we're not contemplating any further branch closures ... in the short term" Airey said.

He said the bank would seriously consider future acquisition opportunities but declined to say whether it currently had any particular target in mind. "If there was another business which made sense from our shareholder's perspective to acquire and it was at the right price, the Bank of Melbourne would obviously give it serious consideration," he said.
Airey would not comment on whether he considered BOM to be a takeover target or if it had been approached regarding a merger.
"Those situations you deal with on a case-by-case basis," he added.
Airey said the bank's wholesale funding would be about 37 percent of total funding by the end of the first half.
"That's still a very sound prudential split between wholesale and retail," he said.

Airey said most of the group's debt issuance for the current fiscal year would come in the second half and would be used to roll over about A$400 million worth of debt maturing in early fiscal 1997/98.
"(The maturing debt) comes up in about July, August of next year and we'll probably come to the market in the April, May, June period of next year," he said.
Airey said BOM was not looking to securitise its A$9.4 billion loan book.
"We've been examining the securitisation option and at this stage we do not believe that securitistion would be a better option," he said.
"The way we're managing our capital and our fund raising is creating greater shareholder value than securitisation."
Airey said the performance of BOM's loan book to date was excellent but the bank would not scrutinise bad and doubtful debt levels until the end of the year.
-- Melbourne Bureau 61-3 9286-1435
